title: The Effects of Lantana camara L. on Soil Physicochemical Properties in the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa
content:
ABSTRACT

Lantana camara L. is an invasive alien plant species that is recognised globally due to its extensive distribution and negative impacts on species diversity and ecosystem dynamics. Despite its extensive distribution in South Africa, its physicochemical impacts on soils are understudied. This study investigated the impacts of L. camara on soil physicochemical properties at three different sites in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. Soils were collected under and at the edge of the canopies of L. camara plants, as well as some distance from the study species. The soils were assessed for soil moisture content, penetration resistance, infiltration and water repellency over four seasons and for pH and soil nutrients once in autumn. The results show that L. camara altered some soil physical properties, but not chemical properties. Lantana camara invasion significantly lowered soil penetration resistance compared to sampling positions away from L. camara plants. Soil infiltration rates showed significant differences between the various sampling positions, with faster infiltration rates at L. camara canopy and edge positions than sampling positions away from the plant across all seasons except in summer. Significant variations in soil water repellency were noted during summer only. Slightly repellent soils were common in spring, but in summer, they were underneath and away from L. camara. The magnitude and direction of these changes differed based on seasonality and sample location. We conclude that L. camara invasion significantly altered the soil physical properties, which may create an environment that favours its own growth and survival. Given the reported effects of L. camara invasion on soil physical properties, it is recommended that L. camara be managed through clearing, even when the changes appear relatively minor.
